questions.stem: A 44-year-old man came to ophthalmology OPD with C/O vision loss for the past few weeks. Fundus examination revealed Bull’s eye maculopathy. On history taking, the patient said that he had been taking some medication for the past three years. Which drug on chronic use would have caused this fundus change?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chloroquine
  • Prolonged use of high doses of Chloroquine may cause vision loss due to retinal damage. Fundus examination shows Bull’s eye maculopathy. Corneal deposits may also occur & affect vision but are reversible on discontinuation, unlike irreversible retinal

questions.stem: A 10-week pregnant woman came to the OPD with C/O intermittent fever, chills & increased sweating. The laboratory investigations showed that she was suffering from Plasmodium vivax malaria. The drug of choice for this patient is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Chloroquine

Vivax malaria during pregnancy can be treated with chloroquine as in non-pregnant, but radical cure with primaquine should be postponed till after delivery, as it is implicated in hemolysis.



Goodman & Gilman’s The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 981, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 877, 885, 890

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female diagnosed with malaria was given a drug for the treatment of malaria. After a few days, she came to the casualty with C/O profuse sweating, giddiness & palpitations. Her blood glucose level was 48 mg/dL. Which anti-malarial drug would have caused this?
questions.solutionHtml:
Quinine
  • The patient came to the casualty with C/O profuse sweating, giddiness & palpitations. Her blood glucose level was 48 mg/dl. This shows that she has hypoglycemia. That is why quinine infusion should be given in D5.
  • Quinine will cause delirium, fever, tachypnoea, respiratory depression, pulmonary edema, hypoglycemia, marked weakness & prostration.


Goodman & Gilman’s The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 975, 976, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology by KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 883, 885

questions.stem: A 10-week pregnant woman came to the OPD with C/O intermittent fever, chills & increased sweating. The laboratory investigations showed that she was suffering from Plasmodium falciparum malaria. The drug of choice for this patient is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Quinine
  • Falciparum malaria during pregnancy
  • Quinine 600 mg TDS × 7 days + clindamycin 300 mg TDS/QID (20 mg/kg/day) for 7 days can be used during all trimesters & is a safer option during 1st trimester.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old male came with C/O intermittent fever, chills & abdominal pain. Peripheral blood smear showed the presence of malarial parasites. The drug of choice for exo erythrocytic stage of this parasite is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Primaquine
  • Primaquine is the drug of choice for the exo erythrocytic stage of the malarial parasite.

questions.stem: A 41-year-old female diagnosed with malaria has been treated with an anti-malarial drug. The doctor advises the patient to take this drug with fatty food or milk. Which of the following drug would have been prescribed to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lumefantrine
  • Lumefantrine must be administered with fatty food/ milk, which markedly enhances its absorption & ensures adequate blood levels. Failure to take it with fat-rich food limits absorption & may result in recrudescence.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male diagnosed with malaria 3 days back has been under chloroquine therapy for the past 3 days. Now the doctor prescribes him the drug Primaquine for the radical cure. Which other drug can be used for the radical cure?
questions.solutionHtml:
Tafenoquine
  • Tafenoquine is similar to Primaquine, and it has been recently approved for the radical cure of malaria. It has a long plasma t½ of 14–19 days (t½ of primaquine is 6–8 hours). Thus, a single dose is enough for the radical cure, whereas primaquine has to be given for 14 days.
